title: Cross-tenant retry amplification investigation and per-tenant adaptive admission control
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A recurring spike of 5xx errors and long tail timeouts was reported by multiple customers over the last 48 hours. Initial traces point to cross-tenant retry amplification originating at the edge admission layer: when a subset of tenants hit sustained slowdowns (KV cache misses + CPU-bound kernel path), upstream clients aggressively retried which amplified load and caused downstream queues to saturate. This produced a feedback loop: timeouts -> retries -> queue growth -> more timeouts.

Hypothesis:
- Edge/frontdoor is not enforcing per-tenant inflight limits; bursty tenants can monopolize router threads and downstream execution slots.
- KV cache compaction/eviction during surges is causing expensive cold-path model initializations which increase p95 latency for other tenants sharing the same pool.
- SDK/client retries are too aggressive in the absence of explicit 429/Retry-After signaling and are amplifying transient failures.

Investigation performed so far:
- Correlated tenant-level traces with queue-depth metrics and kernel CPU heatmaps. Observed clear alignment between tenant bursting and server queue growth across multiple AZs.
- Reproduced a scaled-down scenario in staging by replaying recorded production traffic for 3 tenants; confirmed that one noisy tenant can cause >3x p95 increase for co-located tenants.
- Verified no global circuit-breaker was tripping; circuit thresholds are global not per-tenant.

Short-term mitigations (hotfixes):
1) Deploy edge-side short-term admission controller patch (edge-proxy) to apply a conservative per-tenant inflight cap (default 50 concurrent requests) and early-fastfail when reached. This reduces queue churn and gives slow tenants informative 429 responses.
2) Adjust SDK guidance and temporary rate-limiting rules to reduce client retry aggressiveness (increase backoff window + random jitter).
3) Turn on targeted KV cache prefetching for highest-traffic tenants to soften cold-starts in the next 24h window.

Planned long-term fixes:
- Implement adaptive per-tenant admission control in the edge router with token-bucket shaping that adapts to observed p95 latency and retry rate per tenant. The controller will scale quota up/down on a 60s cadence and expose metrics for audits.
- Add tenant-scoped circuit-breakers and a graceful degradation path that prefers lower-cost cache-backed model variants when latency budgets are tight.
- Make retry guidance explicit by returning Retry-After and structured error codes when admission drops are intentional. Coordinate SDK releases to honor Retry-After headers.
- Improve KV cache eviction policy to be workload-aware (favor hot prefixes for stable tenants) and expose cache occupancy by tenant to the console.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag the admission control behind a rollout flag.
- Canary: enable for 5 non-critical tenants with high traffic (selected by SEs) for 12 hours. Monitor: per-tenant RPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth, retry rate, and customer-visible errors.
- If metrics show regressions, rollback to previous admission thresholds and iterate. Full rollout expected over two weeks after canary if stable.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for token-bucket and admission logic.
- Staging replay with >1M requests/hour to verify queue behavior under burst patterns.
- Chaos tests: randomly delay backend response to validate early-fastfail semantics and ensure no client-side deadlocks.

Observability additions required:
- Tenant-level queue-depth and inflight counters on the edge router.
- New SLO dashboard tile showing tenant-top contributors to p95 latency and retry amplification index.
- Alerting: page when a single tenant accounts for >30% of total queue depth for >5 minutes.

Post-incident follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Run a root-cause postmortem (owner: Marco Ruiz) and update runbook to include admission controls and SDK retry guidance.
- Product to review quota defaults and communicate available controls to customers (owner: Linh Nguyen).
- Research/Applied ML to explore cache eviction improvements and prioritized prefix retention (owner: Priya Mehta).

Notes for customer communication:
- Provide transparent explanation: we observed amplified retries causing transient overload; we implemented admission limits and will roll out adaptive shaping to prevent recurrence.
- Offer remediation: temporarily migrate at-risk customers to dedicated pools or increase their reserved capacity while we finish rollout.
